intro: Lesson 4: Stonehenge: a mystery from above. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: What is Stonehenge?
points: Built in stages from about 3000 BC

panels.title: The view from above
points: A circle inside a ditch and bank

head: Theory
Evidence for it
rows: lines up with sunrise and sunset in summer and winter
many animal bones from feasts nearby

bullets: It lines up with midsummer sunrise
We do not know for certain

keywords.def: a building or structure built to remember or mark something
a circle of huge stones in Wiltshire
an idea that tries to explain something

questions.q: What does the aerial photo show that the ground photo does not?
questions.a: The circle shape, the ditch and the Avenue

questions.q: Where did the bluestones come from?
Do we know for certain why it was built?
Core: Draw a simple plan of Stonehenge from the aerial photo and label the stone circle, ditch and Avenue.
Extend: Choose one theory and give its evidence.
questions.a: For example: a calendar, because it lines up with the midsummer sunrise

questions.q: Stretch: Why can we never be sure?
questions.a: The builders left no writing, so we only have clues
A) From above. Aerial means from the air, looking down.

questions.q: Big question: why drag huge stones so far?
questions.a: It must have been very important to them, perhaps as a calendar, burial or meeting place; we do not know for certain
